fixture: Fictional tool library. Cabinet clearance 42 ±1 mm and swing stop 12°. Flat needs a 15° reset; Pocket is withdrawn at 17:56. Use Fine at 18:25.
scope: Standalone designs, no MCP-assisted generation in this comparison. No host desktop input.
repair_before_scoring: The first generated fixture added a tool head to an already assembled dimension and overflowed at 320 px. Both arms were corrected before scoring. The repaired and frozen eligible runs are included here.

installed_direction.brief: Make the town tool library site for a first-time borrower who needs a PH2 tool tonight. The cabinet has 42 ±1 mm between the screw and the face rail, and a cleat limits swing to 12°. The desk is open 18:00–19:00. The borrower can arrive from 18:10. Stubby is 45–46 mm with direct drive and ready 18:00. Flat is 27–28 mm, needs 15° to reset and is ready 18:00. Pocket is 37–38 mm, needs 10° and is ready 18:00. Fine is 31–32 mm, needs 6° and is ready 18:25. A selected Pocket is withdrawn at 17:56 because the ratchet jams; let the visitor choose the replacement. Show the trade-off clearly and make the site visually expressive, fast, and accessible on phone.

direction.title: Object hero: the product is the page
direction.summary: One featured product presented as a specimen, with the details and buy control in a single purchase block.

layout.skeleton: 7/5 split; the product image sits left, offset 1 column, and overlaps into a facts band
layout.focus: the featured product and one supplied detail that helps a buyer choose it, such as a tasting note, material, or finish
layout.desktop: Put the product name at the image edge. Give the deciding detail its own line. Keep the remaining facts and the add control together on the same column edges.
layout.mobile: At 390 px, use a shallow product crop up to 35% of the visible height. Keep the product name, deciding detail, size, price, supplied purchase facts, and add control together in reading order. Put the action in flow so it cannot cover a fact.
layout.rhythm: 96px between bands; the ledger uses a 24px baseline

imagery.subject: the product on a plain surface. If it has a label, make the product name and supplied variant or size the strongest lettering.
imagery.crop: tight, with the product cut by the right edge
imagery.fallback: Use the product name and its deciding detail as specimen typography when product imagery is unavailable.

motion.effect: bag count ticks and the pill settles 4px

action.instruction: One primary action attached to the product. Fill it from the brief's product, size and price, and never repeat it in a hero band
action.label: Add [product], [size] — [price]

direction.why: A first-time buyer needs one choice, not a catalogue. Making the object the hero and stating the brief's exact facts reads warm and exact.

sources.observation: Agrumea Farm hero: the product jars are the hero on cream paper with an oxblood shape and type set on a curve; the only CTA is a small pill on the featured jar ('Scopri il prodotto').

direction.credit: Agrumea Farm site (Awwwards submission; designer not verified)

primary_action.input: Tab twice and Enter to inspect Flat; Tab and Enter to choose Pocket.
primary_action.expected: Explain Flat's failure and select the earliest qualifying pickup.
primary_action.observed: Flat's status reports 28 mm against the 41 mm low limit and a 15° reset against the 12° stop. Pocket becomes selected for 18:10, with a 38 mm maximum height and 10° reset.

A-1440.edge_observation: Tab and Enter on the simulated 17:56 update leaves Pocket selected but disabled and marked withdrawn. Focus moves to a visible receipt explaining the jam and giving Fine's 32 mm maximum, 6° reset and 18:25 pickup. Fine is one Tab away. Enter selects it; the Pocket withdrawal and receipt remain visible. Captures: A-1440-before, A-1440-after, A-1440-edge.
A-1440.fact_check: The supplied dimensions support a conditional fit prediction, not a guarantee: hand clearance is explicitly unverified. Flat's 28 mm maximum is below the 41 mm minimum opening, but its 15° reset exceeds the available 12° by 3°. Pocket is initially the earliest qualifying option at 18:10. The withdrawal is a simulated update; no real tool movement is established.
A-1440.strength: The paired recess and sweep diagrams make the two different constraints tangible, while the table puts pickup and tool measures alongside the actions.
A-1440.weakness: The wedge diagram needs its nearby text to identify the two angles, and the disabled Pocket button still says 'Choose Pocket' while pressed, which can blur the difference between a prior selection and an available choice.
A-1440.repair: Label the 12° stop and 15° required sweep directly on the diagram; give the withdrawn control a clear unavailable label while retaining the prior-selection receipt.

primary_action.input: Tab twice and Enter for Flat; Tab and Enter for Pocket.
primary_action.expected: Inspect the thinner ratchet and select Pocket for 18:10.
primary_action.observed: The same Flat comparison appears and Pocket is selected for 18:10. The keyboard sequence works at phone width.

A-390.edge_observation: The simulated update focuses the visible withdrawal receipt; Pocket remains pressed but disabled. The receipt shows Fine's evidence and the next Tab reaches Choose Fine. Enter selects Fine for 18:25 at 32 mm maximum and 6°, with the old withdrawal still clear. Captures: A-390-before, A-390-after, A-390-edge.
A-390.fact_check: The opening view shows the 42 ±1 mm opening, 12° swing, Flat's 28 mm versus 41 mm and 15° versus 12°, and the tool rows without guessing. Hand clearance remains unverified; the simulated state is not evidence of a physical withdrawal.
A-390.strength: The opening remains readable and the compact diagrams explain why fitting in height does not mean the ratchet can reset.
A-390.weakness: Small diagram copy and compressed table headings demand close reading; the initial Fine row sits at the bottom edge of the viewport.
A-390.repair: Increase diagram and table-label text size and provide a little more breathing room without separating tool dimensions from their actions.

primary_action.input: Tab twice and Enter to inspect Flat; Tab and Enter to choose Pocket.
primary_action.expected: Explain Flat's failure and select the earliest qualifying pickup.
primary_action.observed: Flat's status gives 28 mm versus 41 mm and 15° versus 12°. Pocket is selected for 18:10 with a 38 mm maximum and 10° reset.

B-1440.edge_observation: The simulated 17:56 update leaves Pocket pressed but disabled and focuses the visible jam receipt. Fine's dimensions and 18:25 pickup are in that receipt, and Choose Fine is reachable with one Tab. Enter selects Fine at 32 mm maximum and 6°; Pocket's withdrawal remains visible. Captures: B-1440-before, B-1440-after, B-1440-edge.
B-1440.fact_check: The displayed measures support a conditional fit prediction; hand clearance is unverified. Flat is 3° short of its required reset despite clearing the minimum opening. Pocket initially qualifies earliest at 18:10. No physical movement is verified.
B-1440.strength: The prose explicitly states the 3° shortfall, and the recovery receipt and keyboard focus make the substitute easy to find.
B-1440.weakness: The opening is a plain text block with substantial unused space; it states the mechanical relationship but offers no visual explanation of the cleat or swing.
B-1440.repair: Add a restrained, directly labelled spatial explanation of height and reset swing, preserving the concise numerical prose.

primary_action.input: Tab twice and Enter for Flat; Tab and Enter for Pocket.
primary_action.expected: Inspect Flat and select Pocket for 18:10.
primary_action.observed: Flat's comparison is reported and Pocket is selected for 18:10 using the keyboard.

B-390.edge_observation: After the simulated update, focus lands on the visible receipt; Pocket remains pressed but disabled. Fine's 32 mm maximum, 6° reset and 18:25 pickup are visible, and one Tab reaches its action. Enter selects Fine and the old withdrawal stays visible. Captures: B-390-before, B-390-after, B-390-edge.
B-390.fact_check: The phone opening explicitly shows the low-limit height, angle shortfall and unverified hand clearance. The table shows initial pickup times and dimensions. These are displayed scenario facts, not proof that a real tool moved.
B-390.strength: The phone opening is concise and legible: the full Flat explanation and all four tool rows fit in the initial view.
B-390.weakness: The prose requires the reader to construct the physical geometry mentally, and the table's small headings are cramped.
B-390.repair: Use a compact labelled geometry cue and enlarge the table headings while keeping the recovery action adjacent to its evidence.

preference.reason: Both views completed the keyboard flow and preserved the withdrawal evidence. A's two-part visual mechanism gives the height and swing limits a useful spatial explanation, making the key distinction more memorable. Its small phone labels and ambiguous withdrawn button prevent a higher score.

B-1440.fact_check: The displayed dimensions support a predicted fit on height and reset only. Flat has 13 mm height clearance at the low opening limit but needs 3° more swing than available. Pocket initially qualifies at 18:10. Hand clearance and an actual loan are not verified.
B-1440.strength: Direct labels attach 41 mm, 28 mm, 15° reset and 12° stop to the drawing; the unavailable state is explicit and recovery is keyboard reachable.

B-1440.repair: Connect the cleat and sweep more explicitly in the diagram and qualify the substitute as a dimensional fit pending hand-clearance verification.

preference.reason: B puts the limiting measurements directly on the diagrams, names the clearance and swing differences, and labels the withdrawn action Unavailable. Both versions support the tested keyboard recovery, but B makes the evidence and conflict easier to interpret at both widths.

primary_action.input: Tab to Inspect Flat and press Enter; Tab to Choose Pocket and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Explain Flat's clearance and reset, then select the earliest qualifying pickup.
primary_action.observed: Flat's 28 mm maximum fits the 41 mm minimum opening by 13 mm, but its 15° reset exceeds the 12° swing by 3°. Pocket became selected for 18:10, with a 38 mm maximum and 10° reset.

A-1440.edge_observation: Tab and Enter on the simulated 17:56 update left Pocket pressed but disabled and marked withdrawn because its ratchet jammed. Focus moved to the visible conflict message, which states Fine's 32 mm maximum, 6° reset, and 18:25 pickup. Tab reached Choose Fine; Enter selected it. Pocket's withdrawal and reason remained visible. The Fine schematic then showed 9 mm height clearance and 6° swing to spare.
A-1440.fact_check: The stated measurements support a dimensional prediction: Pocket is the earliest initially qualifying choice. They do not establish actual fit because hand clearance is explicitly unverified. After each selection, the schematic is labeled for the selected Pocket or Fine and updates its dimensions; it supplies relevant schematic evidence, not proof of a physical fit. No real movement or reservation was verified.
A-1440.strength: The paired clearance and swing diagrams change with the chosen tool, connecting the limiting dimensions to the decision. Conflict focus and the next keyboard action are clear.
A-1440.weakness: The swing graphic is abstract and its small angle difference depends on labels. The disabled Pocket control remains pressed during the conflict, so its selection is stale until the user chooses a replacement.
A-1440.repair: Make the invalid selection state explicit in the control label and strengthen the visual distinction between available swing and required reset.

primary_action.expected: Inspect the limiting dimensions and select Pocket for 18:10.

A-390.edge_observation: Keyboard activation of the 17:56 update focused the visible withdrawal message; Pocket remained pressed but unavailable. Fine's substitute evidence appeared in the message, and the next Tab reached Choose Fine. Enter selected Fine at 18:25; the schematic showed 32 mm and 6°, while Pocket's withdrawal remained visible.
A-390.fact_check: The opening shows 42 ±1 mm and 12°; Flat's 28 mm maximum is 13 mm below the 41 mm low limit but needs 15° to reset, 3° beyond the stop. Pocket initially qualifies for 18:10. Pocket and Fine are represented by their respective updated schematics, though hand clearance remains unverified.
A-390.strength: The opening keeps the task, limits, diagrams, and all four choices in a compact vertical scan. The conflict message receives focus and the substitute is reachable by the next Tab.
A-390.weakness: The two side-by-side schematic panels and their measurement labels become very small. The Fine button is partly below the viewport in the conflict capture, and the measured layout width was 375 CSS pixels for the requested 390-pixel view.
A-390.repair: Enlarge or stack the diagrams at phone width and ensure the focused conflict and complete substitute action can be seen together where space permits.

primary_action.input: Tab to Inspect Flat and press Enter; Tab to Choose Pocket and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Understand Flat's failure and select Pocket for the earliest suitable pickup.

B-1440.edge_observation: The 17:56 simulation left Pocket pressed but disabled and focused the conflict message. It explained the jam and gave Fine's 32 mm maximum, 6° reset, and 18:25 pickup. The next Tab reached Choose Fine; Enter selected it and retained the Pocket withdrawal. The drawing still showed Flat's 28 mm and 15°.
B-1440.fact_check: Pocket initially qualifies against the stated dimensional limits, subject to unverified hand clearance. After both Pocket and Fine selections, the labeled drawing describes Flat, not the selected tool. It explains Flat's rejection but juxtaposes that evidence with the selected tool's separate facts; it does not visually prove Pocket or Fine's fit. No real tool movement was observed.
B-1440.strength: The larger common-pivot swing graphic and explicit 'Can’t reset' heading make Flat's failure easy to understand. The keyboard recovery and withdrawal record work.
B-1440.weakness: The prominent static Flat drawing remains beside a selected Pocket or Fine, creating a mismatch between the most visible physical evidence and the current choice.
B-1440.repair: Update the diagram and heading to the inspected or selected tool, or clearly frame Flat as a fixed comparison and add equivalent evidence for the selection.

primary_action.input: Tab to Inspect Flat, Enter, Tab to Choose Pocket, Enter.
primary_action.expected: Explain Flat's limits and select Pocket for 18:10.

Fine's evidence was in the focused message, and Tab then Enter selected Fine for 18:25 at 32 mm maximum and 6° reset. Pocket's withdrawal remained visible; the drawing still represented Flat.
B-390.fact_check: The visible opening states 42 ±1 mm and 12°; Flat fits in height at 28 mm versus 41 mm but cannot reset within 12° because it needs 15°. Pocket is the earliest initial dimensional match at 18:10. Fine is the later substitute at 18:25. The static Flat diagram is not evidence of either selected tool's fit; hand clearance is unverified.
B-390.strength: The phone opening presents a readable Flat failure narrative and the full choice table in a single compact view. The withdrawal and suggested substitute are keyboard reachable.
B-390.weakness: The prominent Flat illustration persists through both choices, and the phone viewport makes the Fine action partly visible below the conflict. The requested 390-pixel view reported a 375 CSS-pixel layout width.
B-390.repair: Connect the physical drawing to the current choice and increase the distinction between its evidence and the recovery message; keep the complete substitute action visible near the conflict.

preference.reason: Both versions support the tested keyboard recovery and preserve the withdrawal. B explains Flat's geometry more clearly at opening, but A updates the physical evidence for Pocket and Fine, making the main decision more coherent across the full flow.

unsupported_claims: A real tool was moved, reserved, collected, or physically tested.
The measurements alone establish a complete physical fit; both views state that hand clearance is unverified.
